html:
try something on

试穿

The assistant brought another pair so I could try them on.

结构：try + 衣物 + on；代词必须置中：try them on

易错：代词不能放最后说try on them；名词可说try on the shoes。

鞋与购物：用实际使用解释价值和服务 →

fit comfortably

尺寸合适且穿着舒服

The larger pair fitted comfortably from the start.

结构：物品 + fit + 副词

易错：fit comfortably强调穿着尺寸感；suit my style是符合风格，不等于鞋码正确。

鞋与购物：用实际使用解释价值和服务 →

set money aside for

为某用途留出钱

I set a little money aside for a better pair.

结构：set + money/金额 + aside for + 用途

易错：save money可指省钱或储蓄；set money aside for更明确指专门留作某用。

鞋与购物：用实际使用解释价值和服务 →

talk someone through the options

逐项向某人解释选择

She talked me through the options without rushing me.

结构：talk + 人 + through + 选项/步骤

易错：through不是to；talk to me仅表示与我交谈，未说明解释了选项。

鞋与购物：用实际使用解释价值和服务 →

let someone finish

让别人把话说完

I let her finish before asking my question.

结构：let + 人 + 动词原形

易错：let后不用to finish；过去式let形式不变。

礼貌与倾听：让互动中的动作支持评价 →

show an interest in

表现出对……的关注

He showed an interest in how the machine worked.

结构：show an interest in + 名词/动词-ing

易错：注意介词in；be interested in与show an interest in结构不同但都自然。

礼貌与倾听：让互动中的动作支持评价 →

ask someone to clarify

请别人讲清楚

I asked him to clarify the last step.

结构：ask + 人 + to clarify + 内容

易错：ask him clarify缺少to；clarify是动词，不要直接说make clear him。

礼貌与倾听：让互动中的动作支持评价 →

bring a conversation to a close

把谈话自然收尾

I thanked her and brought the conversation to a close.

结构：bring + 谈话 + to a close

易错：close在此是名词；更简单的end the conversation也完全可用。

礼貌与倾听：让互动中的动作支持评价 →

used to dislike

过去不喜欢

I used to dislike soft cooked carrots.

结构：used to + 动词原形

易错：不是used to disliked；be used to eating表示习惯吃，含义不同。

果蔬与口味：从儿时偏好讲到现在的选择 →

have a crunchy texture

有脆的口感

I like apples that have a crunchy texture.

结构：have + a/an + 形容词 + texture

易错：texture是口感/质地；不要把crunchy直接当“甜”的同义词。

果蔬与口味：从儿时偏好讲到现在的选择 →

buy small amounts at a time

每次少量购买

I buy small amounts at a time because my fridge is small.

结构：buy + small amounts + at a time

易错：at a time指每一次；on time指准时，不能互换。

果蔬与口味：从儿时偏好讲到现在的选择 →

go to waste

被浪费、未被用上

I plan a few meals so the vegetables don't go to waste.

结构：物品/食物 + go to waste

易错：不是go to wasted；waste在短语中为名词。

果蔬与口味：从儿时偏好讲到现在的选择 →

catch someone's attention

吸引某人的注意

The folding demonstration caught my attention.

结构：catch + 所有格 + attention

易错：attention不可数；不说catch my attentions。过去式是caught。

广告：区分吸引注意、记住内容与相信信息 →

make a claim about

对……提出某种主张

The advert made a claim about how long the lamp would last.

结构：make a claim about + 内容

易错：claim在这里是尚需判断的主张，不自动等于已证实的fact。

广告：区分吸引注意、记住内容与相信信息 →

check the details

核对具体信息

I checked the details before ordering.

结构：check + the details；可接before + 动词-ing

易错：check和look at不完全相同；check强调核实，而非只看一眼。

广告：区分吸引注意、记住内容与相信信息 →

be put off by

因……而失去兴趣

I'm put off by adverts that interrupt a video too often.

结构：be + put off by + 因素

易错：put off doing可表示推迟做事；be put off by在此表示反感或退缩。

广告：区分吸引注意、记住内容与相信信息 →

a sheet of paper

一张纸

I drew the route on a sheet of paper.

结构：a/two + sheet(s) of paper

易错：表示纸材料时不说a paper；但a research paper可指一篇研究论文。

纸张与手写：把工具的用途和限制说清楚 →

jot something down

快速记下

I jotted the number down before I forgot it.

结构：jot + 内容 + down；代词置中

易错：代词应说jot it down；不是jot down it。

纸张与手写：把工具的用途和限制说清楚 →

sketch out an idea

粗略画出或列出一个想法

We sketched out the idea before opening the design software.

结构：sketch out + 想法/计划

易错：sketch out强调初步轮廓，不表示已经完成了精细成品。

纸张与手写：把工具的用途和限制说清楚 →

keep a record of

保留……的记录

I keep a record of the changes in a notebook.

结构：keep a record of + 内容

易错：record在此是名词；a record与records都可，但须与句子数量一致。

纸张与手写：把工具的用途和限制说清楚 →

struggle with

在某方面遇到困难

I struggled with organising my notes.

结构：struggle with + 名词；struggle to + 动词

易错：with后用名词或-ing；若接原形要换成struggled to organise。

中学与学技能：说明困难怎样被拆解 →

break something down into steps

把任务拆成步骤

She broke the task down into three manageable steps.

结构：break + 任务 + down into + 步骤

易错：过去式broke；break down在其他语境可指设备坏了，需看宾语。

中学与学技能：说明困难怎样被拆解 →

show someone how to

给某人示范怎样做

He showed me how to label the diagram.

结构：show + 人 + how to + 动词原形

易错：how to后不使用过去式；不是showed me how labelled。

中学与学技能：说明困难怎样被拆解 →

get the hang of

逐渐掌握做法

I gradually got the hang of choosing the main points.

结构：get the hang of + 名词/动词-ing

易错：of后用choosing；表达掌握诀窍，不自动表示已达到专家水平。

中学与学技能：说明困难怎样被拆解 →

put a name to a face

想起某张面孔对应的名字

I recognised him but couldn't put a name to the face.

结构：put a name to + a face

易错：不是give a name to his face；这里表达记起身份，不是给人取名。

名字与人物介绍：建立联系并承认记忆边界 →

associate something with

把某事与……联系起来

I associate her name with the painting she showed us.

结构：associate + A + with + B

易错：使用with；不要直接把associate with当成所有情境都等于“联想”，它也可指交往。

名字与人物介绍：建立联系并承认记忆边界 →

make someone feel at ease

让某人放松、不拘束

Her friendly introduction made me feel at ease.

结构：make + 人 + feel + at ease

易错：make后用feel原形；不是made me to feel。

名字与人物介绍：建立联系并承认记忆边界 →

look up to someone

敬重某人

I look up to her because she treats beginners patiently.

结构：look up to + 人

易错：to不可省；look someone up常表示查找某人信息，意思不同。

名字与人物介绍：建立联系并承认记忆边界 →

weigh up the options

权衡几个选择

I weighed up the options before choosing the shorter course.

结构：weigh up + options/选择

易错：这里weigh意为权衡，不是量体重；过去式weighed。

决定与成功：把目标、困难和结果串起来 →

set a realistic goal

设定符合实际条件的目标

We set a realistic goal for the first month.

结构：set + a + 形容词 + goal

易错：realistic不等于容易；目标仍可有挑战，但应联系可用条件。

决定与成功：把目标、困难和结果串起来 →

stick with a plan

持续执行某计划

She stuck with the plan even when progress was slow.

结构：stick with + 名词；也可stick to a plan

易错：过去式stuck；stick with说明坚持，不代表任何情况下都不能调整。

决定与成功：把目标、困难和结果串起来 →

pay off

努力产生好结果

His regular practice paid off during the event.

结构：努力/准备 + pay off

易错：此用法无需宾语；pay off a loan是还清贷款，含义不同。

决定与成功：把目标、困难和结果串起来 →

keep track of

持续掌握进度或信息

She keeps track of the tasks in a shared list.

结构：keep track of + 任务/时间/变化

易错：keep track of与lose track of相对；不要机械翻译为keep the tracks。

有条理的人：用可见习惯解释可靠 →

prioritise the tasks

按重要或紧急程度安排任务

We prioritised the tasks that depended on other people.

结构：prioritise + 名词

易错：prioritise不只是做清单，还包括决定先后；美式拼写prioritize同样正确。

有条理的人：用可见习惯解释可靠 →

leave room for changes

为变化保留余地

Her schedule leaves room for unexpected changes.

结构：leave room for + 名词/动词-ing

易错：room在这里表示余地，不可数；不是leave rooms。

有条理的人：用可见习惯解释可靠 →

follow through on a promise

兑现承诺

He follows through on his promises to the team.

结构：follow through on + 承诺/决定

易错：follow up是跟进，follow through on强调把承诺落实；不宜混作完全相同。

有条理的人：用可见习惯解释可靠 →

overlook a garden

面向并可俯看花园

The reading room overlooks a small garden.

结构：房间/窗户/建筑 + overlook + 地点

易错：这里overlook是俯看；也可表示忽略，需由宾语和语境判断。

城市空间：用声音、布局与活动形成画面 →

be packed with

挤满……

The entrance was packed with visitors.

结构：be packed with + 人/物

易错：packed强调很满；不能用它仅表示有几个人，也不等于一定吵闹。

城市空间：用声音、布局与活动形成画面 →

hear someone over the noise

在噪声中听见某人

I could barely hear my friend over the music.

结构：hear + 人 + over + 噪声

易错：over在此表示压过背景声；不是hear about the noise，后者是听说噪声。

城市空间：用声音、布局与活动形成画面 →

provide a place to

提供可做某事的场所

The garden provides a place to sit between appointments.

结构：provide a place to + 动词原形

易错：to后用sit；provide people with a place是另一合法结构。

城市空间：用声音、布局与活动形成画面 →

pay attention to detail

留意细节

She pays attention to detail when arranging the photographs.

结构：pay attention to + 名词；detail整体可不加s

易错：to是介词；若后接动作可说pay attention to keeping the edges straight。

摄影、手工与历史兴趣：用做事过程描述热情 →

experiment with

尝试不同材料、方法或设置

He experiments with different angles before taking a picture.

结构：experiment with + 名词/动词-ing

易错：experiment here不一定是正式科学实验，也可指创作试验；不要因此虚构实验结论。

摄影、手工与历史兴趣：用做事过程描述热情 →

piece together a story

根据零散资料逐步还原故事

She used old photographs to piece together the street's history.

结构：piece together + 信息/叙述

易错：piece在此作动词；拼接资料不等于所有细节都已确定，应承认缺口。

摄影、手工与历史兴趣：用做事过程描述热情 →

be made from

由某材料制作而来

The cover was made from discarded cardboard.

结构：成品 + be made from + 材料

易错：made from常强调制作来源，made of常强调能识别的构成材料；两者有语境重叠，不是一刀切规则。

摄影、手工与历史兴趣：用做事过程描述热情 →

live up to expectations

达到预期

The film didn't live up to my expectations.

结构：作品/体验 + live up to + expectations

易错：to不可漏；expectations是本人预期，不自动证明作品客观好坏。

采访与电影：把内容理解和个人评价分开 →

find something hard to follow

觉得某内容不易理解或跟上

I found the sudden changes in time hard to follow.

结构：find + 宾语 + hard to follow

易错：是内容hard to follow，不说I am hard to follow来表达自己听不懂；后者会说自己难被理解。

采访与电影：把内容理解和个人评价分开 →

give an insight into

使人了解某方面

The interview gave me an insight into the editing process.

结构：give an insight into + 内容

易错：介词into；an insight也可复数insights，不能写a insight。

采访与电影：把内容理解和个人评价分开 →

come across as

给人留下某种印象

The speaker came across as thoughtful and willing to reconsider.

结构：人 + come across as + 形容词/名词

易错：这是呈现给你的印象，不等于已证实其私下性格；come across a book则是偶然发现书。

采访与电影：把内容理解和个人评价分开 →

get together

相聚

We got together for a simple dinner after the course ended.

结构：人 + get together；可接for + 活动

易错：过去式got；get-together带连字符时也可作名词“聚会”，语法位置不同。

朋友、聚会与快乐：用互动细节建立记忆点 →

bring back memories

唤起回忆

The photograph brought back memories of our rainy picnic.

结构：事物 + bring back + memories

易错：过去式brought；bring back someone可指带某人回来，需看宾语。

朋友、聚会与快乐：用互动细节建立记忆点 →

make everyone feel included

让每个人觉得被接纳并参与其中

She asked each person for a story to make everyone feel included.

结构：make + 人 + feel + included

易错：included是被包含/接纳的状态；including不能替代此处过去分词。

朋友、聚会与快乐：用互动细节建立记忆点 →

have something to look forward to

有一件值得期待的事

Our monthly dinner gives us something to look forward to.

结构：have + 事物 + to look forward to

易错：look forward to里的to是介词；接动作应为look forward to meeting，而不是meet。

朋友、聚会与快乐：用互动细节建立记忆点 →

hand something back

把某物还给原持有人

The tutor handed our essays back on Friday.

结构：hand something back

易错：代词须放中间：hand them back；hand in 表示提交。

课堂通知：日期、数字与澄清请求 →

be meant to do

按安排应该做

We are meant to read chapter four before class.

结构：be meant to do

易错：meant 后接 to + 动词；不是 mean doing 的“意味着”。

课堂通知：日期、数字与澄清请求 →

catch what someone said

听清对方的话

I did not catch the room number. Could you repeat it?

结构：catch what someone said

易错：此处 catch 不是抓住物体；听懂和同意并不相同。

课堂通知：日期、数字与澄清请求 →

share something with someone

与某人共用／分享

Can I share this textbook with you today?

结构：share something with someone

易错：使用 share ... with；不要写 share to someone。

课堂通知：日期、数字与澄清请求 →

involve someone in doing

让某人参与做某事

We involved volunteers in choosing the workshop topics.

结构：involve someone in doing

易错：in 后接名词或动名词：in choosing，不是 in choose。

会议分工：谁提出顾虑，谁负责执行 →

be responsible for

负责某事

Ravi is responsible for booking the meeting room.

结构：be responsible for

易错：for 后的动作使用 booking；responsible 不是动词。

会议分工：谁提出顾虑，谁负责执行 →

specialise in

专门从事／擅长某领域

The trainer specialises in helping new teams communicate.

结构：specialise in

易错：in 后接领域或动名词；美式 specialize 也正确。

会议分工：谁提出顾虑，谁负责执行 →

make the most of

充分利用已有机会或资源

We made the most of the short meeting by preparing questions.

结构：make the most of

易错：保留 the；不等于拥有最多数量。

会议分工：谁提出顾虑，谁负责执行 →

clear up

天气转晴／某问题澄清

The weather should clear up by late afternoon.

结构：clear up

易错：天气语境是变晴；不要机械理解成打扫。

天气播报：地区、时间与例外条件 →

isolated showers

局部零星阵雨

There may be isolated showers near the hills.

结构：isolated showers

易错：isolated 限定分布；不能改述成持续、普遍降雨。

天气播报：地区、时间与例外条件 →

throughout the day

在整天期间

Light rain continued throughout the day.

结构：throughout the day

易错：throughout 强调遍及某时间段；不等于 by the end of。

天气播报：地区、时间与例外条件 →

make way for

让位于／被随后事物替代

The morning mist made way for sunshine.

结构：make way for

易错：made way for sunshine 不表示阳光造成雾。

天气播报：地区、时间与例外条件 →

be absorbed in

全神贯注于

I was absorbed in drawing a map and forgot the time.

结构：be absorbed in

易错：in 后接名词或动名词；不要写 absorbed on。

讲座导入：定义、例子与后文路线 →

lose track of time

忘记时间的流逝

She lost track of time while repairing the bicycle.

结构：lose track of time

易错：lose 的过去式是 lost；常用 track 不加 the。

讲座导入：定义、例子与后文路线 →

in other words

换句话说

The task needs no equipment; in other words, you do not need any tools or devices to do it.

结构：in other words

易错：应保持同一意思，不能用它连接无关的新论点。

讲座导入：定义、例子与后文路线 →

be associated with

与……相联系

The course is associated with practical skills.

结构：be associated with

易错：association 不等于因果证明；with 后接关联对象。

讲座导入：定义、例子与后文路线 →

leave something unchanged

让某物保持不变

The designers left the main entrance unchanged.

结构：leave something unchanged

易错：unchanged 不是没存在过；leave 的过去式 left。

城市绿化：区分反证与尚未提供的信息 →

despite + noun / -ing

尽管存在某情况

Visitors stayed outside despite the light rain.

结构：despite + noun / -ing

易错：despite 后不直接接完整句；可用 although it rained。

城市绿化：区分反证与尚未提供的信息 →

maintenance costs

维护成本

The club needs to budget for maintenance costs.

结构：maintenance costs

易错：maintenance 不可直接作动词；maintain 是动词。

城市绿化：区分反证与尚未提供的信息 →

expand a scheme

扩大一项计划

The school may expand the scheme to other classes.

结构：expand a scheme

易错：expand to 指扩展到某范围；不得把计划写成已完成。

城市绿化：区分反证与尚未提供的信息 →

pay a deposit

支付押金

Customers pay a deposit before borrowing a tool.

结构：pay a deposit

易错：deposit 在此可退押金，不一定是商品最终价格。

循环消费：摘要填空与加工流程 →

remove something from use

停止使用某物

The staff removed the cracked cup from use.

结构：remove something from use

易错：from 后接状态；remove 不必总翻译成物理搬走。

循环消费：摘要填空与加工流程 →

undergo an inspection

经过检查

Each repaired bicycle undergoes an inspection.

结构：undergo an inspection

易错：undergo an inspection 指接受检查；pass an inspection 指检查合格。inspection 是名词，inspect 是动词。

循环消费：摘要填空与加工流程 →

under all conditions

在所有条件下

The method does not work under all conditions.

结构：under all conditions

易错：all 是强限定，不应把某次成功改写成普遍有效。

READING PASSAGE 3

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 27-40, which are based on Passage 3 below.

Book review: The World of Sugar by

UlbeBosma

Ulbe Bosma's The World of Sugar is a genuinely global history. Bosma discusses all the sugar­ growing places of the world, beginning with Cuba and Java, the largest exporters of the early 20th century. But this is a history not just of cane sugar but also of beet sugar, an equally important form of traded sugar over the last hundred years. Beet sugar is grown mainly in Europe and the United States. It has also been massively subsidised and sold at artificially low prices on world markets, threatening the livelihood of producers of cane sugar.

Bosma's discussion of the sugar market in Britain gives a sense of the book's range. The sweet-toothed British first bought cane sugar from their own slavery-dependent colonial plantations. Following the abolition of slavery in the British Empire, cane sugar was imported to Britain from places which retained the practice, such as Cuba and Brazil. Towards the end of the 19th century, the British started to import beet sugar from continental Europe. Only in the 20th century was there a move to develop a national beet sugar industry.

The book provides a global labour history, investigating the wide range of labour regimes associated with growing sugar. Contrary to popular belief, cane sugar production was never just restricted to large, dedicated plantations owned by rich men. For example, in Java, a huge exporter of sugar in the early 20th century, sugar cane was grown together with rice in an extraordinarily labour-intensive way by small farmers.

The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

原文 · 印刷页26

But sugar production was never just a matter of agriculture. It also involved the extraction, close to the place of harvest, of sucrose from the sugar plant, a process which required machinery powered by humans, animals, wind or steam. Further processes involved boiling (from the 19th century, this often involved vacuum systems) and the separation of sugar from other materials in a process known as refinement. From very early on, sugar production was an energy-intensive industrial process, mostly taking place in the countryside and in refineries in centres of consumption, both small and large. The growth of the industry entailed a very rapid diffusion of ideas and techniques from one country to another. Cuba, for example, developed an extraordinarily dense system of railways to transport workers and cane, as well as steam-powered sugar factories. Particular varieties of cane sugar and beet sugar spread very rapidly across the world, in accordance with local needs and demands.

Where once only tiny quantities of sugar could be produced, now new techniques, varieties, fertilisers, irrigation systems and much more have turned gleaming white sugar into a ubiquitous chemical. Over the same time, there has been a massive increase in consumption. Once regarded as a luxury, sugar came to be promoted as a valuable source of energy. But as the consumption of sugar has increased, so has the harm it does, whether to people's teeth or weight. In the face of appalling obstruction from the sugar industry to attempts to reduce consumption, some countries have been forced to tax sugar in order to bring that about. The sugar industry has a history of attacking its critics and, when it comes to obesity, of trying to blame fats, and lack of exercise and self-control. And the recent past has seen worrying new developments in mass sweetening. High-fructose corn syrup made from maize using an enzymatic process invented in Japan in the 1960s has a similar number of calories to table sugar but is far cheaper to produce. It is now widely consumed, having been adopted in the making of soft drinks and a large number of processed foods, and is regarded as a leading cause of obesity.

This is a wonderfully rich book, a model of global history, the history of production and the history of capitalism. Bosma avoids outbursts of emotion, celebratory or critical, even if they might have made his analysis of the multiple tragedies involving sugar all the more powerful. He shows that we could always have done without sugar and that today we have many alternative sources of sweetness. Yet many of the poorest people in the world still depend on it to make a living.
